decisions.rationale: Leading Swampert and Pelipper immediately sets up Drizzle and activates Swift Swim for Mega Swampert, giving it top speed on the board to threaten Garchomp and Talonflame. Archaludon and Tsareena in the back provide crucial typing coverage, with Archaludon resisting Serperior's Leaf Storm and abusing 1-turn Electro Shot in Rain, while Tsareena blocks priority with Queenly Majesty.

Strategic Facts:

decisions.rationale: Serperior Focus Sash Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert; Manectric Magnet Thunderbolt OHKOs Pelipper, so lead deletes rain core before Swift Swim moves. If Swampert Protects, Manectric still removes Pelipper and Serperior finishes next turn. Talonflame provides Tailwind if Swampert remains or speed control; Garchomp checks Archaludon/Pelipper and absorbs Electro Shot. Avoid Garchomp vs Draco.
decisions.notebook: Verified: Manectric Magnet Thunderbolt in rain OHKOs Pelipper. Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert/Mega Swampert but is 90% accurate; it survives Swampert Ice Punch/High Horsepower and can retry. Garchomp Rock Slide does not OHKO Pelipper; EQ does not reliably OHKO Swampert/Archaludon, and Archaludon Draco OHKOs Garchomp (even at -1 SpA it can), so send Garchomp only vs weakened Archaludon or after Snarl/Taunt/Protect. Manectric Lightning Rod absorbs Electro Shot. Swampert High Horsepower OHKOs Manectric, Wave Crash OHKOs Talonflame, Ice Punch can OHKO Garchomp. Pelipper Hurricane can KO Serperior through sash range; Manectric resists. Tsareena survives rain Fire attacks; Brave Bird can KO but is priority-blocked by Queenly Majesty; use Flare Blitz if forced, Glare/Taunt, or focus fire after Pelipper is gone. Mimikyu has Disguise+Focus Sash: Taunt Trick Room and break layers with attacks. Slowking Sludge Bomb can break Serperior's sash; Taunt its Trick Room. Plan: lead Serperior+Manectric vs rain core; double attack unless Swampert Protects, then Thunderbolt Pelipper and finish Swampert with Serperior. Bring Talonflame for Tailwind if Swampert remains or opponent has speed control; Garchomp for Archaludon/Pelipper chip. Do not use Earthquake with Manectric adjacent; Talonflame is immune.

decisions.rationale: Swampert Mega Evolves and Protects to safely block 4x Leaf Storm while establishing Swift Swim in Rain for Turn 2. Pelipper switches to Archaludon, which quad-resists Leaf Storm (0.25x) and resists Electric/Fire, safely taking minimal damage and preserving Pelipper for Rain reset. Next turn Mega Swampert outspeeds the entire opposing team.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon's 100%-accurate Flash Cannon guarantees a KO on Serperior (which dealt 56% on Turn 2 and is now at 44% HP), eliminating opponent's main threat (+2 SpA). Quad-resist Archaludon easily survives +2 Leaf Storm in Rain (20-32% damage). Tsareena uses Wide Lens Power Whip (93.5% accuracy) into Manectric for 59-145% damage, avoiding High Jump Kick crash risk if Manectric Protects. Removing Serperior paves the way for Swift Swim Mega Swampert to sweep the remaining roster.

Leaf Storm at Tsareena pushes Serperior to +4 SpA via Contrary (52-95% next turn vs Tsareena). Snarl goes before Archaludon, dropping SpA so Flash Cannon only does 28-40%—Serperior at 44% survives. Without Snarl, Flash Cannon KOs ~85% of rolls. Double-targeting Tsareena with Flamethrower doesn't guarantee the KO (combined 54-100% vs 77% HP) and leaves Serperior exposed. Snarl also chips both foes and preserves Manectric as an Electro Shot absorber.

Serperior +4 Leaf Storm does 52-95% to Tsareena. Tsareena HJK: 65-93% vs Manectric, 43-63% vs Serperior. Plan: stack Contrary boosts, use Snarl to mitigate Archaludon special hits, switch to Garchomp/Talonflame for Archaludon EQ/Brave Bird when appropriate. Never EQ with Manectric adjacent; Talonflame immune. Tailwind if Swampert remains or speed control needed.

decisions.rationale: Pass with Serperior, replace Manectric with Talonflame. Serperior must stay to threaten Water/Ground and stack Contrary, but needs Protect support. Garchomp's EQ doesn't OHKO +2 Archaludon and Draco can remove it; it also gives no speed control vs Swift Swim Swampert. Talonflame can Protect into Electro Shot, set Tailwind, use priority Brave Bird vs Swampert/Pelipper, and pressure Tsareena. This keeps the sweep alive and handles rain speed war.
decisions.notebook: Verified: Manectric Magnet Thunderbolt in rain OHKOs Pelipper. Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert/Mega Swampert (90% acc) and survives one Ice Punch from full; Contrary turns Leaf Storm drops into +2 stages, cap +6. Garchomp Life Orb Earthquake vs +2 Def Archaludon is only a 2HKO at best, especially spread; Archaludon Draco Meteor at -1 SpA can still OHKO Garchomp. Archaludon Electro Shot in rain executes in one turn and can OHKO Talonflame; Protect scouts it. Talonflame Tailwind is the main answer to Swift Swim Swampert; Brave Bird has +1 priority from full HP via Gale Wings and is not blocked by Queenly Majesty unless targeting Tsareena. Flare Blitz in rain is only neutral vs Grass but can finish weakened Tsareena. Pelipper can block Garchomp EQ by immunity/Wide Guard and may set opposing Tailwind; Serperior Leaf Storm is neutral and can OHKO Pelipper with enough Contrary boosts. Swampert raw Speed in rain ranges 180-244, so Serperior usually needs Tailwind. Plan: keep Serperior protected from Archaludon Flash Cannon/Electro Shot; use Talonflame Protect/Tailwind to scout and gain speed; bring Garchomp later to EQ Archaludon or Swampert, but beware Draco and Ice Punch. Avoid Earthquake when an immune/friendly slot would be problematic; Talonflame is immune to Ground. Against Mimikyu/Slowking-Galar: Taunt Trick Room, break Focus Sash carefully; Slowking Sludge Bomb can break Serperior sash.

decisions.rationale: Tsareena uses Protect to stay alive at 16% HP and maintain Queenly Majesty passive pressure. Archaludon uses Flash Cannon on Serperior (9% HP) to guarantee a KO (deals 13.7-30.7%). Serperior's +4 SpA Leaf Storm does 27.9-53.3% to Archaludon (77% HP), so Archaludon comfortably survives any attack. Removing Serperior clears the way for Mega Swampert to sweep under Rain.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Switching Tsareena to Pelipper provides a clean immune switch-in to Garchomp's Earthquake while resetting Rain for 8 turns with Damp Rock. Under Rain, Archaludon's Electro Shot executes in a single turn, gaining +1 Special Attack before firing into Talonflame for a likely OHKO or severe damage. Archaludon comfortably survives Garchomp's Earthquake with +2 Defense, triggering Stamina for +3 Defense. With Talonflame threatened and Pelipper's Wide Guard available next turn, we secure complete control.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Archaludon)
decisions.rationale: Garchomp's only attacking moves (Earthquake and Rock Slide) are both spread moves, which are completely blocked by Pelipper's Wide Guard. Archaludon uses super-effective STAB Draco Meteor on Garchomp to secure the win.

Last mon standing. Archaludon is locked into Electro Shot (immune vs Garchomp) this turn, so it's safe. Rock Slide is the only move that can hit Pelipper (EQ immune). At 58% HP, Rock Slide has ~49% KO chance (40.7-74.8% dmg). Garchomp outspeeds both foes. Swords Dance is futile since +2 EQ still can't guarantee OHKO on +2 Def Archaludon, and Draco Meteor OHKOs Garchomp next turn regardless. Maximize damage now.
decisions.notebook: Series strategy for Game 3: Opponent core is Pelipper/Archaludon/Swampert-Mega/Tsareena. Archaludon with Stamina is the biggest threat—physical hits boost its Def, making it nearly unbreakable from Garchomp. Draco Meteor from Archaludon OHKOs Garchomp (120-173%). Must handle Archaludon with special attacks or focus it before Stamina stacks. Pelipper's Wide Guard blocks spread moves (EQ/Rock Slide)—bait it or use single-target moves. Hurricane is 100% accurate in rain. Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert; Contrary boosts make it snowball. Manectric Thunderbolt in rain OHKOs Pelipper. Priority: eliminate Archaludon early before Stamina accumulates; avoid repeated physical contact. Tsareena at low HP is easy cleanup. Watch for opposing Tailwind speed control. Garchomp outspeeds Archaludon and Pelipper but not Mimikyu/Slowking if brought.

reflections.summary: Won Game 2 and the series 2-0. The team-preview plan and draft registration were highly effective: bringing Mega Swampert, Pelipper, Archaludon, and Tsareena completely countered the opponent's build. Archaludon's Stamina walling Manectric, Tsareena absorbing Serperior's Leaf Storms while blocking Gale Wings priority, and Pelipper's Wide Guard shutting down Garchomp's spread attacks secured total board control.
reflections.adjustment: Maintain the same bring of Mega Swampert, Pelipper, Archaludon, and Tsareena for future rematches. Navigating the early game by protecting Swampert from Serperior and rotating in Tsareena/Archaludon remains the optimal game plan.

Strategic Facts & Prep Conclusions:
- Mega Swampert in Rain outspeeds their entire team and threatens OHKOs across the board.
- Tsareena's Queenly Majesty shuts down Talonflame's Gale Wings priority.
- Pelipper's Wide Guard neutralizes Garchomp's Earthquake and Rock Slide entirely.

reflections.summary: Lost game 2 and the series mainly at team-preview/prep level rather than from flagged in-turn errors. The four brought were poorly suited to the opponent’s rain core: Manectric’s Electric attacks fed Archaludon’s Stamina, Serperior’s Grass pressure was absorbed by Tsareena, and Garchomp’s physical spread offense ran into Wide Guard before being removed by Draco Meteor. We evolved no Mega of our own, while opponent’s Swampert Mega was pivotal. The between-game idea to prioritize Archaludon was right, but the personnel and execution backfired because the selected team lacked the proper special/Steel-tolerant answers.
reflections.adjustment: In a future rematch, do not use Manectric as the primary Archaludon answer and do not rely on Garchomp spread physical moves while Pelipper can block them with Wide Guard. Force Pelipper out or use single-target pressure before committing to Rock Slide/Earthquake, and focus Archaludon with special attacks before Stamina stacks. Reconsider bringing registered Aegislash or Rotom-Wash over Manectric/Garchomp if their sets can better handle Archaludon or rain. Expect immediate Swampert Mega evolution, Damp Rock rain, Protect scouting, and possible Trick Room variants if Mimikyu or Slowking appear.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s durable plan: Pelipper sets Damp Rock rain, protects spread moves with Wide Guard, and enables Mega Swampert and Archaludon. Archaludon is the central win condition: Stamina converts many resisted/physical interactions into Defense boosts, Leftovers gives longevity, Flash Cannon is repeated pressure, Electro Shot is dangerous in rain, and Draco Meteor removes Dragon-weak targets. Tsareena resists Grass, can Protect-bait, and punishes frail Electric attackers with Power Whip. Opponent may use Protect early to scout and preserve Mega Swampert. Prep conclusion: avoid physical/Stamina trades, avoid spread moves until Wide Guard is accounted for, and bring special pressure or Steel-resistant answers; Serperior can threaten Swampert but needs help against Tsareena/Archaludon, while Manectric is a poor Archaludon answer. Unregistered Mega Floette, Spiritomb, Overqwil, and Absol have no shown evidence of fixing this matchup.
